description: Patient demographics, medical history, allergies, medications - fields vary widely per patient
read_write_pattern: Read-heavy, occasional structured updates, needs flexible schema
rationale: Patient records have a semi-structured, evolving schema (not every patient has the same fields), so a document model avoids constant schema migrations while still allowing indexed queries.

description: Continuous heart-rate, SpO2, and blood-pressure readings from bedside/wearable monitors
read_write_pattern: Extremely write-heavy, time-ordered, queried by time range
rationale: Vital-sign streams are high-frequency, append-only, and queried by patient + time range, which matches Cassandra's partitioned, time-ordered wide-row model.

description: Relationships between doctors, specialists, hospitals, and patient referrals
read_write_pattern: Multi-hop traversal queries, e.g. 'find a specialist reachable through my GP's referral network'
rationale: Referral and provider networks are inherently relationship-centric, so a graph database gives efficient traversal for referral chains, fraud detection, and network analysis.

description: X-ray, MRI, and CT scan image/DICOM files linked to a patient record
read_write_pattern: Write-once, read-many, large binary objects delivered via CDN/PACS
rationale: Large binary imaging files are best stored as objects keyed by patient/study ID rather than inside a database record, with lightweight metadata pointers kept in MongoDB.
